title: Length skein bucketing & pad-delta optimizer for microbatch shaping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Optimize micro-batch shaping by grouping concurrent requests into 'length skeins' (multi-dimensional bucketing) and introducing a pad-delta optimizer that reduces unnecessary padding across prefill and decode phases. Goal is to improve token throughput and P50/P95 latency for mixed-length workloads without regressing quality.
background: We observed elevated padding overhead with current seqlen bucketizers under mixed traffic (short chat turns + long generation prefill). Existing bucket strategies trade simplicity for wasted tokens on GPU. Prior work (ENG-4721, ENG-9142) reduced padding at coarse granularity but left gaps in prefill->decode transitions where padding is reintroduced due to kernel affinity constraints and KV-cache alignment requirements.
goals: 1) Reduce average padded tokens per request by >=20% on representative enterprise workloads; 2) Keep P50 latency within 5% of baseline and improve P95 by 10% where padding was dominant; 3) Maintain stable kernel selection decisions and avoid oscillation that causes tail latency spikes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end benchmark on chat-sim workload shows >=20% reduction in padded tokens and >=8% improvement in token/sec GPU utilization
No functional change in outputs (sanity diffs)<1% for sampled eval prompts
New metric pad_delta is emitted to runtime tracing and Grafana dashboard
Can toggle pad-delta optimizer off via runtime flag without requiring model restart
Unit and integration tests cover kernel hint paths and prefill/decode alignment logic
design_summary: We introduce a two-stage optimization: (A) length skeins: a multidimensional bucketing that groups requests by (prefill_length_bucket, decode_length_hint, kernel_preference) to preserve kernel affinity while exposing finer-grained packing opportunities; (B) pad-delta optimizer: a lightweight solver that, given a skein composition, computes minimal per-request pad adjustments (trim/extend) that maximize slot utilization constrained by KV-cache alignment and attention-window kernel constraints. The system prefers small trims on prefill tokens that are unlikely to impact model output (prompt trailing whitespace, assistant meta tokens) and extends only short requests to avoid fragmentation when doing so improves global utilization.
implementation_tasks: Spike: synthetic workload generator and profiler for skein composition (Asha) - 2d
Scheduler: add skein grouping step in request ingress pipeline (Marco) - 3d
Pad-delta solver: greedy + ILP fallback implementation with time budget guard (Katherine) - 3d
Kernel hints: map skein -> kernel candidates and record affinity in request metadata (Marco) - 2d
KV-cache alignment: extend prefill/trim policies to produce safe KV offsets (Infra) - 2d
Metrics & tracing: add pad_delta, skein_size, and pad_savings to tracing schema and Grafana (Observability) - 1d
E2E tests: add model-level deterministic tests and perf harness (QA) - 2d
Docs & runtime flag: CLI/Console toggle + rollout notes (Docs) - 1d
experiments: Spike results (2026-02-22): synthetic mixed-chat workload (50% short 8-32 tokens, 50% long 256-1024 tokens) showed naive skein grouping reduced padding 14% with no kernel hints; adding pad-delta greedy solver improved reduction to 26% but introduced a 3% P95 latency jitter when aggressive ILP fallback was enabled.

Kernel mapping experiment (2026-03-03): pinned kernel affinity per model family; this reduced tail oscillation but required fallback heuristics when GPU memory fragmentation prevented requested kernels.
A/B test plan: run pad-delta optimizer on 10% of production traffic for 48h, compare pad_savings and latency tails before expanding to 30%.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gate off in runtime 1.23; 2) Canary: enable for internal staging and job-sim traffic; 3) A/B 10% production for 48h while monitoring pad_savings, P50/P95 latency, error rates; 4) Expand to 50% if no regressions; 5) Full rollout with opt-out runtime flag
risks: Over-aggressive trimming causing semantic regressions in prompts (mitigation: conservative default trim whitelist + eval checks)
Solver-induced latency if ILP fallback runs frequently (mitigation: time budget and greedy-first policy)
Kernel affinity oscillation causing cache misses and tail latency (mitigation: hysteresis and affinity cooldown)
Complexity increase in request ingress could add maintenance burden (mitigation: encapsulated module with small public surface)
Interaction with Dedicated pools where customer pinned kernel variants require strict behavior (mitigation: honor customer pin as hard constraint)
open_questions: Q1: What is an acceptable trim whitelist for customer-owned prompts? Need legal/PM guidance
Q2: How should we surface pad_delta impact in Console cost breakdowns? (PM input required)
Q3: Should pad-delta adjustments be logged in plaintext traces for debugging, or redacted for privacy? (Security review)
Q4: Are there model families where attention kernel constraints forbid any trimming? Need research input
